Description: Practice-area anchor links should scroll smoothly to the target section
Do: Use scroll-behavior: smooth on html element

Description: Fixed law-firm nav should not obscure hero or disclaimer content
Do: Add padding-top to body equal to nav height
Don't: Let nav overlap first section content

Description: Current practice-area page/section should be visually indicated
Do: Highlight active nav item with color/underline
Don't: No visual feedback on current location

Description: Clients expect back to work predictably during a client-intake wizard
URLs should reflect the selected attorney/practice-area for sharing
Show client location in the site hierarchy of practice areas
Do: Use for sites with 3+ levels of depth

Description: Too many animations undermine a law firm's authoritative, trustworthy tone
Do: Animate 1-2 key elements per view maximum

Description: Animations should feel responsive not sluggish on a case dashboard
Don't: Use animations longer than 500ms for UI

Description: Respect motion preferences for elder-law and accessibility-sensitive clients
Show feedback during case-dashboard async operations
Don't: Leave UI frozen with no feedback

Description: Hover effects don't work when clients browse the firm site on phones
Don't: Rely only on hover for important actions

Description: Infinite animations distract from serious legal content
Some CSS properties trigger expensive repaints on attorney-profile cards
Do: Use transform and opacity for animations

Description: Linear motion feels robotic on a professional legal site
Do: Use ease-out for entering ease-in for exiting

Description: Stacking conflicts can hide the consultation-booking modal
Hidden overflow can clip required legal disclaimers or attorney-advertising notices
Do: Test all content fits within containers

Description: Fixed elements like a call-now bar can overlap other fixed elements
Do: Account for safe areas and other fixed elements
Code Example Good: Fixed nav + fixed bottom with gap

Description: New stacking contexts reset z-index around the practice-area mega menu
Do: Understand what creates new stacking context
Don't: Expect z-index to work across contexts

Description: Layout shift when attorney headshots load is jarring
100vh can be problematic for full-screen mobile intake screens
Do: Use dvh or account for mobile browser chrome

Description: Legal copy that spans full width is hard to read
Don't: Let text span full viewport width

Description: Small buttons are hard to tap; elder-law and legal-aid clients need larger targets
Adjacent touch targets on a mobile intake form need adequate spacing
Custom gestures can conflict with system navigation in the client portal
Do: Avoid horizontal swipe on main content

Description: 300ms tap delay feels laggy when booking a consultation
Accidental refresh mid-intake loses client answers
Tactile feedback improves confidence when submitting sensitive case details
Do: Use for confirmations and important actions

Description: Keyboard users on legal-aid sites need visible focus indicators
Do: Use visible focus rings on interactive elements

Description: Visual feedback on clickable attorney cards and CTAs
Do: Change cursor and add subtle visual change
Don't: No hover feedback on clickable elements

Description: Show immediate feedback when a client presses Request Consultation
Clearly indicate a disabled Submit until intake consent is checked
Prevent double submission of a free case evaluation form
Do: Disable button and show loading state

Description: Clients need to know when a document upload to the portal fails
Do: Show clear error messages near problem

Description: Confirm a consultation request was received
Do: Show success message or visual change

Description: Prevent accidental deletion of a matter or case document
Legal-aid and government audiences require WCAG AA readable text
Don't convey case-status by color alone (open/closed)
Do: Use icons/text in addition to color

Description: Attorney and office images need text alternatives
Do: Descriptive alt text for meaningful images

Description: Screen readers use headings to navigate practice-area pages
Don't: Skip heading levels or misuse for styling

Description: Icon-only buttons in the client portal need accessible names
The entire intake wizard must be operable via keyboard
Don't: Keyboard traps or illogical tab order

Description: Legal content should make sense when read aloud to immigration clients
Do: Use semantic HTML and ARIA properly

Description: Every client-intake input must have an associated label
Do: Use label with for attribute or wrap input

Description: Intake form errors must be announced to screen-reader users
Do: Use aria-live or role=alert for errors

Description: Let keyboard users skip a nav-heavy practice-area menu
Do: Provide skip to main content link
Don't: No skip link on nav-heavy pages

Description: Large attorney and courthouse photos slow page load
Load below-fold testimonials and case results as needed
Do: Lazy load below-fold images and content

Description: Large bundles slow the initial load of a legal-tech app
Returning clients to the portal should load fast
Serif brand fonts can block rendering of the firm homepage
Chat widgets and analytics can block rendering of the firm site
Large JavaScript slows interaction in a case-management dashboard
CSS/JS can block first paint of the practice-area landing page
Every field on the free case evaluation form needs a visible label
Do: Always show label above or beside input

Description: Intake errors should appear near the field with the problem
Don't: Single error message at top of form

Description: Validate the client's email/phone on the intake form as they go
Do: Validate on blur for most fields

Description: Use appropriate input types on the consultation-booking form
Do: Use email tel number url etc

Description: Help browsers autofill a client's contact details on intake
Mark required intake fields (name, matter type) clearly
Let clients see their password while signing into the secure portal
Confirm the free case evaluation submission status
Intake inputs should look interactive, not like static text
Don't: Inputs that look like plain text

Description: Show the right keyboard for phone/case-number fields on mobile intake
Design the firm site for mobile then enhance for larger screens
Do: Start with mobile styles then add breakpoints

Description: Test the intake flow at all common screen sizes
Mobile layouts for legal-aid users need touch-sized targets
Legal text must be readable on all devices
Set viewport so the firm site renders correctly on phones
Avoid horizontal scrolling on practice-area pages
Attorney photos should scale with their container
Billing line items and matter tables can overflow on mobile
Do: Use horizontal scroll or card layout

Description: Adequate line height improves readability of dense legal copy
Long lines of legal text are hard to read
Consistent type hierarchy aids scanning of practice areas
Brand fonts should load without layout shift on the firm homepage
Body legal text needs good contrast for all clients
Do: Use darker text on light backgrounds

Description: Practice-area headings should stand out from body text
Show system status while legal research results load
Guide users when the matter list has no cases yet
Code Example Good: No matters yet. Open a case!

Description: Help clients recover from a failed document upload
Show progress through the multi-step client intake wizard
Transient confirmations for non-critical portal actions
Confirm a booked consultation to the client
Handle long case summaries gracefully
Do: Truncate with ellipsis and expand option

Description: Use locale-appropriate formats for filing and hearing dates
Code Example Good: Filed 2 hours ago or locale format

Description: Format settlement and billing amounts for readability
Show realistic legal sample data during development
Clients should be able to skip the client-portal walkthrough
Help users find attorneys or case law faster as they type
Dead-end case-law searches frustrate researchers
Code Example Good: Try searching for a related statute instead

Description: Tagging e-discovery documents one by one is tedious
Clients must know a legal AI assistant is not a lawyer or legal advice

Description: Waiting for a full legal research answer is slow
Do: Stream text response token by token

Description: Elements should respond to eye tracking before pinch in a legal spatial app
Case-document panels need Z-depth to separate from the environment
Auto-play firm brand video consumes data and energy
Heavy hero imagery increases the firm site's carbon footprint

Description: Legal AI answers need user feedback to improve
Parallax/scroll-jacking on the firm site can cause nausea
